# SmartDns

> SmartDns is a zero-dependency DNS resolver for Node.js with intelligent caching,
> TTL-aware expiration, request deduplication, optional stale-while-revalidate and
> configurable DNS providers. Written in TypeScript, shipped as ESM and CJS, MIT licensed.

## Links

## Core facts

- Package: [@darcas/smart-dns-promises](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@darcas/smart-dns-promises)
- Repository: [github.com/DarCas/smart-dns-promises](https://github.com/DarCas/smart-dns-promises)
- Runtime: Node.js 20 or >= 22
- Runtime dependencies: none
- License: MIT

## What it does

- Resolves a URL's hostname to an IP address before the HTTP request is made.
- Caches resolved records, honoring the real DNS record TTL clamped to configurable bounds.
- Deduplicates concurrent lookups for the same hostname into a single in-flight resolution.
- Optionally serves stale entries while refreshing them in the background (SWR).
- Remembers failed lookups in a short negative cache to avoid repeated resolver pressure.
- Configures Node.js process-global DNS: providers, custom servers and result ordering.
- Exposes statistics: hits, misses, errors, revalidations and average resolve time.

## Providers

- AdGuard: 94.140.14.14, 94.140.15.15
- Cloudflare: 1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1
- Comodo: 8.26.56.26, 8.20.247.20
- DNS.WATCH: 84.200.69.80, 84.200.70.40
- Google: 8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4
- OpenDNS: 208.67.222.222, 208.67.220.220
- Quad9: 9.9.9.9, 149.112.112.112
- Verisign: 64.6.64.6, 64.6.65.6
- Yandex: 77.88.8.8, 77.88.8.1
- Custom servers via setServers().

## Public API

- SmartDns.factory(provider?, resultOrder?, ttl?, options?)
- dns.resolver(url) -> { address, hostname, urlReplaced }
- dns.setProvider(provider)
- dns.setServers(servers)
- dns.stats -> { hits, misses, errors, revalidations, avgResolveMs }
- SmartDnsProviderError, SmartDnsResolverError
- DnsProvider enum: AdGuard, CloudFlare, Comodo, DnsWatch, Google, OpenDNS, Quad9, Verisign, Yandex
- Options: family, minTtl, maxTtl, negativeTtl, swr, onStats

## Notes

- setProvider, setServers and setDefaultResultOrder mutate process-global DNS behavior
  intentionally. Initialize SmartDns early and avoid conflicting configurations.
- The library sits before the HTTP client; it does not replace it.
